title: Left in charge of the band and the Virgil Williams ledger
summary: When Wynn left, Virgil Williams put Cheatham in charge and paid him by ledger; decades later he learned he was accused of running off with the money, which his friend Duff still believes.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Williams took it over. So when Albert Wynn -- left the Dreamland, he left me there and Virgil Williams and -- put the band in my charge, you know. So naturally I was young, with that job, I didn't know what it was all about, so he wasn't paying, he was getting a band every night and wasn't paying the musicians. He would give me a book at the end of the night -- a ledger and he would give me maybe $20.00. And I'd sign my name at the bottom of this ledger. And I'd give the musicians -- you'd divide it up, whatever it was. And that's the way he was paying off. And I was ignorant of the fact, I didn't know what was happening. Until recently -- before the bass player, Charlie Turner died in New York, he told me, he said, you know, Virgil Williams told all the musicians in Chicago that you ran away from Chicago with the band's money. And I was surprised to hear that and he said because he showed us the books where he paid you in full, what he -- put all the money up at the top of the ledger, but I'd sign on the bottom, so he -- you know I had no receipts, I had no nothing to go by, but I don't think any of the musicians believed it.

The union didn't believe it because they knew this guy was a crook. There was only one guy believed that I ran away with some money and that was my best friend, from Nashville, the drummer, by name of Hosea Jose Duff. Now he -- I brought him to Chicago to play with me in the Dreamland and he, right to this day, believes that I ran away with the band's money.
And you didn't learn this till almost 50 years later?
That's right. That's right. When I was with Benny Goodman I went back to Chicago and I looked up Duff, because we went to school together --

And I called him and I wrote and no answer at all. And I went out to his house and no one was ever home. I went to his son's and no one was ever home, so he didn't want to see me at all. But he still believes that I ran away with the money. That's funny. But --
